# Advanced Database Systems Portfolio – EkoDash Logistics

**Course:** MIT 8103 Advanced Database Systems, MIVA Open University, 2026/2027 First Semester
**Student:** Abdullahi Habiba (2026/A/MIT/0437)
**Repository:** <https://github.com/UIbyBiba/advanced-database-portfolio>

## Selected case study

**EkoDash Logistics Ltd** is a *simulated* last-mile parcel delivery company operating in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt. The company and all of its data are fictional and were generated by the scripts in this repository.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Nature of business** | On-demand delivery: customers book a pickup in an app, a nearby motorbike/tricycle/van rider is assigned, the parcel is picked up, tracked and delivered, and payment is taken by card, transfer, in-app wallet or cash |
| **Users of the database** | Customers (mobile app), riders (rider app), and admin staff: dispatchers, finance, support, super-admin |
| **Major data stored** | Cities and pricing zones; customers and saved addresses; riders and vehicles; delivery orders and their status history; payments; customer and rider wallets with a ledger; ratings; live rider locations |
| **Key operations** | Place and price an order, assign the nearest available rider, update delivery status, take payment and debit/credit wallets, pay riders, rate riders, produce earnings and revenue reports |

The same case study is used in all five activities, building on one data set: 600,000 orders, 50,000 customers and 1,500 riders.

## Repository structure

```
advanced-database-portfolio/
├── portfolio-1-database-design/          ER diagram, schema, constraints, normalisation, data generator
├── portfolio-2-query-optimisation/       6 business queries, before/after execution plans, indexing, analysis
├── portfolio-3-transactions-concurrency/ COMMIT/ROLLBACK, 5 concurrency anomalies reproduced and fixed
├── portfolio-4-nosql/                    MongoDB document model + Redis key-value model, suitability
├── portfolio-5-distributed-cloud/        PG streaming replication & failover, Mongo replica set, sharding, cloud design
├── tools/                                screenshot renderer for the evidence files
└── README.md
```

Each folder has its own `README.md` explaining what was built, how it was tested, the results and how to re-run it. Raw outputs are in each folder's `evidence/` or `results/` directory. The `screenshots/` images are rendered verbatim from those output files by [`tools/render_screenshots.py`](tools/render_screenshots.py).

## Summary of results

| Activity | Headline evidence |
|---|---|
| P1 Design | 12-table BCNF schema; 10/10 rule-breaking statements rejected by constraints |
| P2 Optimisation | Q1–Q3 and Q5 sped up 1,100–3,160×; BRIN index 400× smaller than a B-tree; leaderboard from > 60 s → 1.2 ms via rewrite + materialized view |
| P3 Transactions | Lost update, race condition, non-repeatable read, write skew and deadlock each reproduced with two live sessions, then prevented |
| P4 NoSQL | 203,899 order documents; history query 203,899 → 7 docs examined after indexing; 2dsphere and Redis GEO nearest-rider search |
| P5 Distributed | PG replica failover in 0.11 s; Mongo automatic election with 40/40 writes kept; zone-sharded cluster with single-shard routing |

## Software used

| Software | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL | 16.15 | Relational database (P1–P3, P5) |
| MongoDB | 7.0.34 | Document database, replica set, sharding (P4, P5) |
| mongosh | 2.14.0 | MongoDB shell |
| Redis | 8.10.2 | Key-value store (P4) |
| Python | 3.13.18 | Test harnesses: psycopg 3.3, pymongo 4.19, redis-py 8.1 |
| Mermaid CLI | 11.16.0 | ER and architecture diagrams |
| Playwright 1.63 / Chromium, matplotlib 3.11 | Screenshot rendering, performance chart |

## Quick start

```bash
# Portfolio 1
createdb ekodash
psql -d ekodash -f portfolio-1-database-design/sql/01_schema.sql
psql -d ekodash -f portfolio-1-database-design/sql/02_seed_data.sql

# Portfolio 2
python3 portfolio-2-query-optimisation/scripts/benchmark.py baseline
psql -d ekodash -f portfolio-2-query-optimisation/sql/02_optimisation_indexes.sql
python3 portfolio-2-query-optimisation/scripts/benchmark.py optimised

# Portfolio 3
python3 portfolio-3-transactions-concurrency/scripts/transaction_demos.py
```

For Portfolios 4 and 5, see the README in each folder. They need running MongoDB and Redis servers.
